# Benefits summary - fraud alert triage

*Synthetic data for a fictional UK retail bank. Generated by `src/report.py` - do not edit by hand.*

## Headline (days 31-60, same alerts under both processes)

- **18.5% of alerts (3,278 of 17,764) closed automatically** with a logged reason; 5% of them still go to a person as a quality check.
- **149 investigator hours a week released**, about **4.6 full-time investigators** (at 32.5 productive hours a week).
- **Alerts decided within 24 hours: 84.7% → 96.1%.**
- **Median time to a decision on genuine fraud: 14.8 → 7.7 hours.** The priority queue holds 5% of alerts but **29%** of the fraud.

## The trade-off

- 14 genuine fraud cases (2.0% of 684) scored low enough to be auto-closed; the QA sample caught 1, so **13 would be missed** (98.1% of fraud still reaches a person).
- Before going live, the risk owner would need to agree that trade-off, or lower the auto-close threshold or raise the QA sample.
  Both are single settings in `src/config.py`.

## Rule tuning opportunity

- **R06 Round-amount transfers** creates **22%** of all alerts but finds **3%** of the fraud: only 0.5% of its alerts are genuine, and each case found costs **41 investigator hours**. It is the first candidate for re-tuning with the rule owner.

## Benefits tracking table

| Measure | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Alerts needing an investigator | 17,764 | 14,658 | -3,106.0 |
| Investigator hours | 3,769.7 | 3,131.2 | -638.5 |
| Investigator hours per week | 879.6 | 730.6 | -149.0 |
| Alerts decided within 24 hours | 84.7% | 96.1% | +11.3 |
| Median hours to decision (alerts a person reviews) | 15.0 | 9.2 | -5.8 |
| Median hours to decision: genuine fraud | 14.8 | 7.7 | -7.1 |
| False alarms reviewed by a person | 17,080 | 13,987 | -3,093.0 |
| Genuine fraud reviewed by a person | 684 | 671 | -13.0 |

## Model

Logistic regression on 11 alert features plus the rule that fired, trained on days 1-30 only. AUC on days 31-60: **0.81**. Thresholds were set on days 1-30 and not changed afterwards.
